subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: After the accessor defect is fixed, should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` permanently reject every legacy ownerless session row, leaving recovery to an operator or non-plugin client?
rationale: The mechanical authorization repair is clear, but changing access to persisted rows created before ownership metadata existed is an upgrade-facing security and compatibility policy that repository history does not conclusively settle.

options.title: Fail closed consistently
options.body: Match the strict delete boundary, document or prove the operator/non-plugin recovery path, and require deployed upgrade evidence.

options.title: Add verified ownership migration
options.body: Provide a narrow operator or doctor flow that assigns a known owner before plugin-runtime patch access resumes.

options.title: Coordinate all ownership paths
options.body: Pause until create, patch, and delete share one maintainer-approved ownerless-session contract.

recommendation.title: Fail closed consistently
recommendation.body: Match the strict delete boundary, document or prove the operator/non-plugin recovery path, and require deployed upgrade evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the strongest available history signal for the storage-neutral session projection boundary where the policy must be implemented consistently.
